title: Cache-induced response drift: targeted evals and mitigation guardrails
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We observe diffs in model outputs that correlate with KV/prefix cache hits after changes to runtime config, kernel selection, or model variants. These diffs sometimes alter semantics (e.g., instruction-following or factual answers) and surface as customer complaints or regression alerts. Scope: build a focused evaluation suite and monitoring pipeline that measures semantic drift attributable to cache hits, ties regressions to specific config/model changes, and provides automated guardrails (canary behavior, temporary disablement, or conservative cache invalidation) during rollouts. Goals: 1) Detect cache-hit-induced semantic changes with high precision; 2) Attribute regressions to config/model deltas; 3) Provide low-friction mitigations (automatic fallback to cache-bypass for affected routes, rollout pause).
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible eval harness (prefix-kv-sensitivity-suite) exists that can run on nightly CI and on-demand for any model/config snapshot
Telemetry shows per-route cache_hit flag and per-request semantic similarity metric in the console dashboard
An alert rule triggers when >0.5% of sampled queries exhibit semantic-similarity-drop > 0.08 between cache-hit and cache-miss baselines after a deployment
Canary policy implemented: new runtime/model changes route 5% traffic with cache disabled for 24h and compare metrics; rollout must pass thresholds before ramp
Runbook and rollback steps documented and linked from the alert
proposal: Deliverables: 1) prefix-kv-sensitivity-suite: 2,000 curated prompts across instruction, QA, summarization, and code completion to stress prefix caching; 2) two comparison modes: synthetic (forced cache miss vs hit using controlled inputs) and live A/B (canary with cache bypass); 3) metrics: embedding cosine similarity delta, normalized token edit distance, and log-prob shift summary; 4) dashboards: per-model and per-route comparison charts; 5) automated gating in the deployment pipeline and a temporary runtime toggle to disable prefix cache per-route.
test_matrix: Dimensions: model family (redwood-1.2, open-compat-2.0), quantization profile (fp16,int8), batch sizes (1, 8, 32), sequence lengths (256, 1024, 4096), cache state (cold, warm, warmed-with-different-prefix), update types (kernel swap, compilation flags, model weights, tokenizer changes). For each cell run 200 examples from the suite and compute similarity metrics. Prioritize cells seen in production traffic distributions.
monitoring_plan: Instrument request path to emit cache_hit boolean, prefix_length, route, model_version, runtime_revision. Aggregate daily: fraction of queries with similarity_drop > 0.05 (cache-hit vs cache-miss). Alert when fraction exceeds threshold and when change correlates with a deployment ID. Keep a 30-day rolling window for trend detection. Add a persistent debug log option for flagged routes to capture inputs/outputs for offline triage.
mitigation_strategy: Short-term: automatic route-level cache bypass for affected routes via runtime toggle; conservative fallback to previous model variant for routes with repeated failures. Mid-term: adaptive cache invalidation heuristics (invalidate prefixes when tokenizer changes or model weight delta exceeds threshold). Long-term: integrate cache-safety checks into pre-deploy CI and require canary pass for cache-enabled deployments.

risks: False positives from natural model non-determinism can inflate alerts; similarity thresholds need calibration per workload. Additional CPU cost for running paired cache-miss runs in canary can increase billing. Tokenizer changes can cause apparent semantic drift even when model behavior is unchanged.
